pr_title: Set script execution as cancelled when stopped
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Currently when an automation is running and is stopped by the UI (always stops the current actions) or via a service call (stop actions is optional), the error message is very unclear:
![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/7083755/707babe4-40be-497b-9ac1-e224d6f5e848)
To make it clearer what is happening, I propose to set the script execution status to cancelled when the automation is stopped. This makes a clearer error message, thus giving a better indication on why it exactly failed (for example disabling the automation in a scene which is activated by that same automation, or disabling the automation in the same automation without setting stop actions to false).
![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/7083755/7fe292b0-9669-4206-9c22-0e598e5dfb4a)

issue_context.title: Stopped because of unknown reason "null" at
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Since version 2023.8.x I have an automation that has the following error when it executes with triggers. If I execute it manually then everything works.

Stopped because of unknown reason "null" at 5 août 2023 à 07:05:50 (runtime: 0.19 seconds)_

```yaml
alias: Désactivation mode nuit
description: ""
trigger:
  - platform: state
    entity_id:
      - binary_sensor.mouvement_bureau
      - binary_sensor.mouvement_cuisine
      - binary_sensor.mouvement_salon
    from: "off"
    to: "on"
condition: []
action:
  - service: scene.turn_on
    data: {}
    target:
      entity_id: scene.mode_jour
mode: single
```

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.8.x

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2023.7.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Automation

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments: If you try to run that scene via calling the service in the developer tools, does that work?
Yes no problem with developer tools
can you maybe show the states of the binary sensors in the state overview in developer tools?

I'm not sure to understand what you want ![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/52531214/d4ee4a72-4d2c-46df-a3cf-32aac7ac330e)

The automation start automatically with trigger. 

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/52531214/5c1248c6-93a8-4008-8ec9-ee185a86754c)
Ah allright, this also answers my question, I was trying to break it down into smaller parts to see where the error could be. I'll try if I can reproduce this
I just tried to create a similar automation with a motion sensor and calling a scene as action and for me it seems to work. Can you see anything in the logs?

I think I found the source of the problem. In my scene I desactivate my automation. I deleted this action and I added this action in the automation ![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/52531214/434e650b-d5fc-4542-8e26-431fb91efa5d)
And with the error the automation is desactivated
Can you maybe put your HA to english for the screenshots? I can read a bit of french but English would be easier to read.
Right let me try that as well
Ah that worked. I can reproduce this on my production environment, I'll try to do the same on my dev environment and then I will check where it goes wrong

I also found another bug in the meantime, if you delete an automation, the scene shows an empty list of entities and activating the scene causes an error to log, but I can't update my scene to remove it

So the service to turn off the automation has an argument called "stop actions" which, as the name implies, stops all actions. When you turn off an automation via the UI you always stop the actions (which kinda seems logical to me, because for example you have an automation with a long timer or something similar and if it didn't automatically stop that action when you turn it off you could end up with running this automation 10 times unless you manually call a service to stop everything, you get the point).

So the quick fix for you for now is turning the automation off via the automation itself and then passing false as argument like so
```yaml
action:
  - service: scene.turn_on
    data: {}
    target:
      entity_id: scene.test
  - service: automation.turn_off
    data:
      stop_actions: false
    target:
      entity_id: automation.97828
```

I am still going to try to figure out how we can improve this error message

>  In my scene I desactivate my automation

Why?

If you don't want an automation to execute its `action` for a certain reason, use the automation's `condition` to control when it should, or should not, execute it. That's its main purpose.

You can even use inline conditions (or `choose` or `if`) within `action` to determine which actions get executed.

Similar/the same problem here. I have a script that turns on Spotify in my living room. When I execute it manually or using Siri it works fine. When I execute it from my Philips Hue Dimmer Switch I am getting `Stopped because of unknown reason "null" at 19 August 2023 at 16:37:48 (runtime: 0.80 seconds)`.

I am getting this error on all Spotify-related actions such as `Set source`, `Set volume`, and `Play media`.

Also the `continue_on_error: true` option does not help. The script it still crashing and stopping. See screenshots below.

![Screenshot 2023-08-19 at 4 46 24 PM](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/39517491/74e3b38d-e755-4ea6-97af-ff2c00da3f31)
![Screenshot 2023-08-19 at 4 46 43 PM](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/39517491/42e9ea4e-001b-49c9-a195-4d88525969f9)
Can you create a separate issue?

review_comments:
Stopping a script is not cancelling it. It could be an intended stop.

../Frenck
FWIW It looks like we also set `cancelled` above on line 418 when stop is set causing it to return from that function so it may be wrong in a few places.
I'm making an adjustment to return values when cancelled is raised here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/98501 -- another angle for looking at the same issue.

Reading the code, the only time "cancelled" is used is when "stop" is called. While cancellation seems to be used internally as part of stopping, i'm not sure I see another use of cancellation anywhere.

There is only one use of "cancelled" which is one out of 3 or 4 cases stop is called.

WDYT about:
- introduce a new status `stopped`
- everywhere stop is set, the status "stopped" is set
- Depending on the context, may be able to add additional information to the trace where that stop is called (e.g. it can include the detail that it was stopped because mode: `restart`, or it can do nothing if stop was called externally)
- add a new frontend code "stopped" as well etc
- deprecated cancelled since it seems to be an internal detail

Another option could be to introduce other modes like `failed_restart` that gives a more specific error message for cases we know about where the script is stopped because another automation ran and stopped it.

(I'm not a script expert, but intent is to keep the conversation moving.)

My original idea was indeed to introduce stopped, but then I came across that comment. I think using stopped can be something good.

This is code I never touched so I don't know the ins and outs, but I think having a way to know why something happens would be usefull as well. The bug that made me make this PR, is that the user got a vague error. Even when this is merged, the user can see that it's stopped or cancelled, but still doesn't know why. (Maybe they accidentally left it in a scene? Maybe they are triggering another automation that disables the current one?) Can we find a way to fix this and add room for extending this in the future?
